translation:
In the unborn expanse of the dharmadhātu,
Dwells the Mother, the Noble Lady, Goddess Tārā.
She who bestows happiness upon all sentient beings,
I pray, protect me from every fear!

context: Work: བློ་སྦྱོང་ཚིག་བརྒྱད་མ། (author: གླང་རི་ཐང་པ།). A canonical Tibetan text; the blocks below are being translated one at a time, in order.

translation:
Without realizing that one’s own nature is the dharmakāya,
The mind falls under the power of the afflictions;
To the mother-beings wandering in saṃsāra,
O Mother Goddess, I pray that you protect them.

translation:
Although we abide within the ultimate reality,
Because we do not understand the dependent origination of cause and effect,
And are deluded regarding the nature of all that can be known,
I pray that the Mother, the Goddess of Omniscience, may protect us.

translation:
Characterized by the nature of space, free from conceptual elaboration,
Inseparable from all that exists—
To those of us who are still but trainee individuals,
O Mother, the Perfect Buddha, I pray that you grant protection.

translation: This prayer, known as the "Seven Protections," was offered by the King of Dharma of the three realms, the Victorious Drigungpa, Kyobpa Rje 'Jig-rten-gsum-gyi-mgon-po, when he beheld the seven faces of the Noble Tara in the E-chung cave; it is renowned for its immense blessings.
